mentl/c943a0b:
Per realize protocol's ULTIMATE MEDIUM articulation: the closure IS
the thread record. ONE record, FOUR roles, four-and-a-half (closure +
thread context). No parallel thread-record table; no next_tid counter;
no partition arithmetic.

Substrate cascade:

1. WasiThreads effect trimmed to TWO ops: wasi_thread_spawn(closure_ptr)
   + wasi_num_cores(). Removed: thread_record_alloc / _pack_task /
   _done_addr / _result_addr / _self_id — all collapse into closure-
   record field access.

2. ffi_spawn: closure already exists in heap (LMakeClosure emitted it).
   wasi_thread_spawn(closure_ptr) hands the host the closure; host's
   $thread_start(closure_ptr) reads fn_idx from closure[0],
   call_indirects with closure-as-__state, stores result at
   closure[done_offset+4], atomic.store done=1, atomic.notify.

3. ffi_join: atomic.wait32 on closure_done_addr(closure_ptr); read
   result from closure_result_addr.

4. closure_done_addr / closure_result_addr: pure address-arithmetic
   on the closure record. Layout:
     [fn_idx@0][capture_count@4][captures@8..(8+4*nc)][done@8+4*nc]
     [result@done+4]

5. wasi_threads handler reduced to 2 arms matching the trimmed effect.
   Sentinel intrinsics retained for graceful-degrade under sequential_
   compose dispatch — closure_ptr passes through as Handle payload;
   ffi_join's atomic-wait returns immediately because no thread sets
   done=1 (each branch ran to completion in spawn-site stack frame
   per sequential_compose semantics). Same source, handler swap.

state IS closure IS evidence — spawning a thread doesn't allocate

fields done/result are layout-emitted by the wheel's emit_module
(peer-extension: spawnable closures allocate +12 bytes for these
three fields). Per protocol_bootstrap_wasi_threads_substrate.md.

mentl/c984409:
Both src/backends/wasm.mn::emit_pat_nested_predicate and the seed
mirror bootstrap/src/emit/emit_control.wat::$ec5_emit_pat_nested_predicate
emitted nested-LPCon tag checks via cumulative `i32.and`. WASM's
i32.and evaluates BOTH operands before AND-ing, so the inner
sub-field load (i32.load offset=N) fired even when the outer tag
mismatched — reading offset-N of a sentinel/error-AST that has no
inner field → memory fault on speculative load.

Restructured both to recursive short-circuit form: each LPCon arm
wraps the continuation in `(if (result i32) (then <new check +
recurse>) (else (i32.const 0)))` so inner loads only fire when
outer matched. Mirrors per protocol_emit_is_graph_projection.md;
seed introduces two helper emitters $ec5_emit_if_result_i32_then
and $ec5_emit_else_const_0_close.

link that dies when the phone sleeps is not worth sending. POST /tape
stores a .bmrg in memory under the first 12 hex chars of its SHA-256

clob/c9bc2bd:
Bet 2 asks whether crystallizing prediction errors into ternary residual
modules lowers held-out loss on a substrate that can learn. Every prior
crystallization run was on a random core; Phase 6 produced the first
trained one, so this wires the crystallization loop onto it.

eval::bet2_dense captures the core's own high-error episodes from the
train corpus (post-final-norm hidden, observed future, top-k), feeds them
to the existing CrystallizationEngine with the trained readout as the
token-direction table, then measures the holdout with modules loaded vs
cleared. Because modules apply additively post-final-norm and never feed
back into recurrent state, one forward pass scores both arms: equal
compute is exact and tokens no module routes to are identical between
arms, so drift on untouched inputs is structurally zero. The test lands on
the exact object Phase 6 validated (the dense core's deployed view), not
the tied-readout CoreModel.

DenseModel gains decode_step_capture (returns the pre-unembed hidden),
unembed, and readout/dims accessors; CrystallizationEngine gains
push_module. Mechanism is unit-tested: the cleared arm reproduces the
trusted eval_nll, zero modules is bit-identical, an injected module moves
only the loaded arm, and capture records well-shaped episodes. The
scientific verdict is left to the pre-registered run.
